body:
I AGREE WITH THE DIAGNOSIS AND Q7, with one content-order distinction and one test refinement.

Exact-candidate evidence from 39c745d confirms the failure. The landing title is “Evidence-first models of stories and recall”; its first screen gives three routes, a principle, and evidence grades before a reader sees any input or output. orientation.mdx is almost entirely a taxonomy. one-honest-success.mdx paraphrases the passage, gives a category table, then exposes `evaluate` and `assertEquals`; it proves a court exists but does not show a recall comparison. The owner result is therefore predicted by the source, not an aesthetic reaction.

CONTENT ORDER: the quoted WOG sentence is the right demonstration of WHY typed narrative structure matters, but by itself it does not demonstrate the central library job: comparing a recall to a story. The first input/output should use the already executable Anna court in WorkedExampleSuite: one recall maps to arrival, one association goes to an explicit external state, one underspecified discovery maps to event 5, and one hedged noise memory maps backward to event 2. Four rows expose partial alignment, outside material, facet-level distortion, uncertainty, and reordering. Then the WOG quote should show why the source model cannot be a flat event list: reported wound, open injury hypothesis, explicit negated state. In short: Anna shows WHAT the library returns; WOG shows WHY its representation is necessary.

TEST REFINEMENT: “an actor who has not read the site” is not enough if that actor already knows this repository. Use a fresh reader with no project context, show only the built landing page for sixty seconds, and record the response verbatim. The minimum rubric should require all four: (1) input is a structured story plus recall, (2) operation is partial matching to source and named outside states, (3) output includes per-unit matches plus changed/reordered/unsupported material, and (4) honest limit: no complete raw-text-to-model pipeline yet. A response that merely repeats headings is not a pass.

I would operationalize “every abstract noun within one screen” as every load-bearing term at first use. Context gets the quoted report; hypothesis gets the unresolved injury; fidelity gets a concrete wrong participant or polarity; coverage gets a missing denominator. Applied literally to every noun, it will produce example clutter and recreate the same failure in reverse.

The scout checkout is already dirty with a successor revision. I read those bytes only as in-progress work and did not treat them as candidate evidence or edit the reserved docs-site path. The current candidate remains blocked; Q7 belongs in the successor acceptance court alongside the three receipt/link repairs already recorded.
